title: The Angevins next shut the merchants of al-Andalus out of Flanders
source: Trent's account (8 January 1447); the autosave of 1 February 1447 dates it 7 January

title: Al-Andalus answers the Angevins in kind and closes its markets to their merchants, beside the embargo it has kept on them since 1440

Since 1442 the treasury has gone into the towns, each being made good at a trade: cannon foundries, gunsmiths, saltpetre works, tanneries, masons, glass and pottery, cloth workshops doubled at Qurṭuba and Ishbīliya, and twenty-seven bridges
source: Trent's account (12 November 2026); the buildings from the saves of 11 June 1442, 27 August 1444 and the autosave of 1 February 1447

title: Thirteen years after Temür's death no successor has filled his place, and the Tīmūrid empire turns in on itself and stagnates

data.founder: Emperor Temür Lang Borjigin, 'died 13 years ago' (the game's text)
data.standing: the Tīmūrids are still the world's fourth great power in October 1447, behind China, the Angevins and al-Andalus

source: Trent's screenshot, 27 March 1447; save of 5 October 1447

title: Tunis goes to war with Sicily for Palermo and calls the Emperor to arms. Al-Andalus accepts, and its seven ṭāʾifas come in with it the same day

data.call: Tunis calls upon us to join them in their 2nd Tunis–Sicily War against Sicily, Athens, Negroponte, Genoa, Arborea, Corsica, Cuneo, Gazaria, Dignois, the Papal States and Arezzo. This is a war that they have started (the game's text, as Trent's screenshot shows it)
data.alliesOfTunis: Tripoli, Gabès, Touggourt, Gallura, Annaba, Constantine

source: Trent's screenshot and account, 13 June 1447; save of 5 October 1447

title: A daughter, Fāṭima, is born to Saʿd son of Aḥmad of Banbalūna and Muʾmina daughter of the prince Aḥmad: the Emperor's great-granddaughter, joining the crown's line and the ṭāʾifa's again

data.father: Saʿd ibn Aḥmad (born 27 July 1419), son of Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf, lord of the Ṭāʾifa of Banbalūna
data.mother: Muʾmina bint Aḥmad (born 14 June 1423), daughter of the prince Aḥmad by ʿĀʾisha bint Saʿd

title: The envoys of the Christian princes come to Ishbīliya with gifts and careful compliments. The Emperor answers 'We have arrived': al-Andalus keeps its seat at Europe's table, and opens a claim to the borders of the Umayyad caliphate

data.text: the Christian princes had written al-Andalus off as a chapter concluded; now their envoys come with gifts and careful compliments, curious what the Emperor intends. 'We hold no mastery yet, only a seat regained at a table we once headed... this time we do not mean to leave it' (the game's text)
data.precedent: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān II and the embassy of Theophilos, 840 (the game's historical note)
data.effects: while al-Andalus keeps 25 European dominance for the rest of the Golden Century, it keeps the benefits of the Restoration of al-Andalus; unlocks the casus belli 'Restore the Umayyad Caliphate Borders' and the ṭāʾifa subject type
data.claim: the game's 'Umayyad Caliphate' term: 2,816 locations in 17 areas, among them Sūs, al-Maghrib al-Aqṣā, the Atlas high plateau and the rest of the Maghrib, and five regions: Iberia, the Fertile Crescent, Egypt, Arabia and Persia (Trent's screenshot)

title: At Ozieri in Sardinia Genoa's vassal Arborea, 4,290 men, beats 1,655 of Tunis's vassal Gallura, which loses half its army
Isabel de Montsoriu, wife of the Emperor Muḥammad for more than forty years and mother of the prince Aḥmad, dies of old age on her sixty-fifth birthday
Off the west coast of Corsica two Sicilian ships fall on three of the ṭāʾifa of al-Burtughāl and drive them off without loss
In the Gulf of Termini, off Sicily, six Genoese ships attack the combined fleet of Tunis, Tripoli and Gabès, twenty-eight ships, which loses nineteen of them for one of Genoa's

data.result: allied disaster (the save records the Genoese attack as not carrying the day, but the losses are the allies')

title: At Grasse in Provence Aḥmad, lord of the Ṭāʾifa of Banbalūna, fifty-one years old, attacks 4,200 Genoese with 385 men and loses all but 29 of them

commanders.ours: Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf, lord of Banbalūna

data.afterwards: his command ends that day; the save marks him ruthless

title: The treasury goes into the towns again: six bridges in the country of the Tagus and the Guadiana, at Alcántara, Medellín, Villanueva de la Serena, Valencia de Alcántara, Brozas and Jaraicejo, and new gunsmiths, tanneries, glassworks and a cannon foundry

data.bridges: Alcántara, Medellín, Villanueva de la Serena, Valencia de Alcántara, Brozas, Jaraicejo
data.earlier in 1447: potteries at Valencia, cloth and a tannery at Córdoba, a furniture workshop at Cervera (by 28 March)

source: saves of 1 February (autosave), 28 March and 5 October 1447

title: ʿAbd al-Jalīl al-Qubbāṣī's voyage of discovery ends on 1 October; four days later he sails again for the cape where Africa ends, to find a place to leave an outpost

data.aim: an outpost at or near the cape (Trent)

source: Trent's account, 5 October 1447; save of 5 October 1447
